subject: Music Production
title: Harmonics and Timbre
description: A short lesson to help you apply Harmonics and Timbre.

hook.text: A piano and a violin can play the same note at the same volume and still sound completely different.

buildup.text: The difference is timbre, which comes from additional vibrations called harmonics or overtones.

discovery.text: Every instrument produces a fundamental note plus a unique set of quieter harmonic frequencies.

twist.text: Synthesizers mimic real instruments by recreating their specific harmonic patterns artificially.

climax.text: Producers use equalization to shape harmonics and give each track a distinct character in a mix.

punchline.text: Hidden overtones give every instrument its voice.

quiz.question: What causes a piano and violin to sound different on the same note?
options: Different harmonic overtones creating unique timbre
